title: Sell Mineral Rights in Sheridan County, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Sheridan County, MT
metaDescription: Sheridan County sits on the thin western edge of the Bakken, not the core. I buy mineral interests here based on the honest decline curve, not ND-style hype.
heroLead: I'll say this straight to any Sheridan County family up front: you're on the edge of the Bakken, not in the middle of it, and that difference matters to what your minerals are worth.
intro: I ran wells across the Williston Basin long enough to know exactly where the pay thins out, and Sheridan County sits right at that pinch. The Bakken and underlying Three Forks are real here — there's been genuine horizontal drilling activity along the county's eastern and southern edges since the boom years — but net pay thins noticeably compared to the core counties across the North Dakota line, and well economics reflect it. Fewer wells per section, longer payouts, and operators who've been more selective about where they'll drill.

Underneath that newer Bakken story is an older one most people outside the industry never hear about. Sheridan County had conventional Madison-formation production going back to the original Williston Basin discoveries in the 1950s, long before anyone talked about the Bakken by name. A lot of older family mineral interests in this county trace to leases and severances from that earlier era, layered now under newer Bakken-era leasing on the same legal descriptions.

sections.heading: Why I don't quote Sheridan County like Richland or Williams County, ND
paragraphs: It would be easy to let a family assume their Sheridan County interest is worth what a cousin's Bakken interest in North Dakota core acreage sold for. It isn't, and I won't let that comparison stand uncorrected. Well density here is lower, and a meaningful share of the county's leased acreage was drilled selectively rather than developed on the same tight spacing you'd see closer to Williston. That's not a knock on the county — it's just the honest edge-of-play reality, and it's exactly why I look at your specific unit's actual production rather than county-wide headlines.

sections.heading: The Madison-era layer underneath
paragraphs: If your family's mineral interest was originally leased in the 1950s or 60s for conventional Madison production, that lease may have expired decades ago, or it may have been re-leased when Bakken interest picked up in the 2000s and 2010s. I check both layers of history — the old conventional record and the modern unconventional one — because they can produce very different pictures of what's actually being paid on the same legal description today.

sections.heading: Where the activity actually concentrates
paragraphs: Within Sheridan County, drilling has leaned toward the areas nearer the Bakken's stronger extension rather than spread evenly county-wide. Parcels near Plentywood, Medicine Lake, and the eastern county line have seen more real activity than ground further west and north toward the Saskatchewan border, where interests tend to be quieter and more speculative. I check where your specific section falls in that picture before I say anything about value.

sections.heading: Split-estate and BLM considerations
paragraphs: Some ground in this county carries federally reserved mineral interests from earlier homestead patents, and where that applies, the BLM's own leasing and permitting process runs alongside — sometimes ahead of, sometimes behind — state permitting on adjacent private minerals. If your family's interest sits on split-estate ground, I confirm whether it's state, private fee, or federally administered before I say what I can offer, because those are three different transactions with three different processes.

sections.heading: Heirship across generations of quiet ownership
paragraphs: A fair number of Sheridan County interests I run into trace back to Scandinavian and Central European homestead families who settled this corner of Montana in the early 1900s, with mineral rights passed down through three or four generations since. I regularly find several heirs holding a single fractional interest, most unaware of the others, and I buy directly from any one of them without requiring the whole family to act together.

sections.heading: What I tell every Sheridan County caller upfront
paragraphs: I'd rather lose a phone call to an honest answer than win one with an inflated promise I can't back up once I've pulled the title and production record. That's the standard I hold myself to on every parcel in this county, whether it's a strong Bakken-era interest near Westby or a quiet homestead severance near Redstone.

faqs.question: Is Sheridan County part of the real Bakken boom?
faqs.answer: Part of it, on the thinner western edge. Net pay and well density here don't match the core counties in North Dakota, and I price interests against that honest reality rather than boom-era headlines.

faqs.question: My family's lease is decades old — is it Bakken or something older?
faqs.answer: Possibly conventional Madison-formation production from the 1950s or 60s, later re-leased during the Bakken years. I check both layers of history on your parcel.

faqs.question: Does location within the county matter that much?
faqs.answer: Yes. Activity concentrates more toward the eastern county line and Plentywood, while ground further west and north tends to be quieter. I check your specific section rather than quoting a county average.

faqs.question: How does split-estate or BLM land change a sale?
faqs.answer: It adds a step to confirm whether your interest is state, private fee, or federally administered minerals, since each follows a different leasing and transfer process.

faqs.question: Why should I trust an edge-of-play valuation over a bigger number?
faqs.answer: Because a number that doesn't match the actual production and lease record falls apart during closing. I'd rather quote you accurately the first time.

faqs.question: My family's interest is split among several heirs who've never met — can you still buy my share?
faqs.answer: Yes. I buy individual fractional interests directly and don't require every heir to participate for me to purchase your specific portion.

faqs.question: Are you honest even when the news isn't great for my parcel?
faqs.answer: Yes. I'd rather tell you your interest is quiet ground with modest value than inflate a number that won't hold up once I've done the title and production work.
